🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Harold Greene, the longtime Los Angeles television news anchor whose steady voice guided Southern California viewers through decades of breaking news, has died at 82.

Greene died on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. His daughter, Courtney Greene, confirmed his death in a Facebook post on Wednesday, November 4, writing, "Our beloved husband, father, uncle, and friend has signed off for the last time." She said her mother and she were by his side, adding, "We have a feeling he's already settling into the great newsroom in the sky."

Greene began his career in news as a writer, cameraman and producer in local newsrooms across Southern California, including Los Angeles, Santa Barbara and San Diego, and he was instrumental in forming KCST-TV's news team in San Diego.

He joined KABC in Los Angeles in 1978, left to pursue other opportunities, and returned in 1982, remaining there until 2000. In 2001, he returned to CBS LA, where he spent seven years anchoring alongside Pat Harvey and Ann Martin.

Over his career, Greene won Emmy Awards and three Murrow Awards, and he received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1999.

His family said a memorial will be scheduled after the holiday season.

Rest in Peace, Harold Greene.

Sources: People, confirming his death and his daughter's announcement; CBS LA; KABC.
